stages.title: Calibration
stages.goal: Set up Practice mode and measure the starting point

gate.description: Calibration gate: baseline core blocks done; notation quiz at least 80% over 10 questions

stages.title: Universal defense
stages.goal: Block correctly, break throws, punish on reflex

stages.title: Movement and spacing
stages.goal: Make moves whiff and punish the whiff

gate.description: Movement gate: whiff-punish drill at least 7/10 over 3 sets; sidestep drill at least 7/10 over 3 sets

stages.title: Yoshimitsu core kit
stages.goal: Own the ten core moves, his punishers and his bread-and-butter

gate.description: Core kit gate: BnB 8/10 on both sides over 3 sets on 2 days; punish lab at least 8/10 at -10, -11, -13, -14 and -15; punish quiz at least 90%; missed punishes at most 2.0 per game
Heat gate: one Heat combo 7/10 over 3 sets; Heat wasted at most 40% over 5 Heats; Heat quiz at least 85%
Panic gate: panic-tool success at least 55% over 20 logged attempts; Flash punish lab at least 8/10 against -6 to -9 moves; Flash interrupt drill at least 7/10

stages.title: Stances I: DGF, KIN, NSS
stages.goal: Turn plus frames into stance pressure

gate.description: Stances I gate: stance transitions 8/10; DGF mixup against a random-guard dummy at least 60% hits; stance quiz at least 85%

stages.title: Okizeme and stances II
stages.goal: Convert knockdowns; add FLE, IND, MED, BT and BDS

gate.description: Okizeme gate: oki drill against random wake-ups at least 60% correct; staple combo 7/10; oki conversions at least 0.5 per game

stages.title: Matchups
stages.goal: Beat the characters he actually meets

gate.description: Matchups gate: at least 3 problem moves with answers for each of the 10 most-faced characters; missed punishes at most 1.0 per game; win rate at least 45% against each, with at least 10 games each

stages.title: Mastery
stages.goal: Keep sharp and adapt to patches

gate.description: No gate. Maintenance targets: missed punishes at most 0.5 per game; panic-tool success at least 65%; win rate at least 50% against the top 10 over 20+ games each

nodes.title: Controls and notation
nodes.why: Reading notation is the language every drill, combo and coach answer is written in.

nodes.title: Practice setup
nodes.why: Frame display and dummy recording turn Practice mode into a measuring instrument instead of a guessing game.

nodes.title: Baseline assessment
nodes.why: The baseline measures which parts of the old Tekken 7 skill survived the layoff, so placement is earned, never assumed.

nodes.title: Guard levels
nodes.why: Blocking the right height is the whole of defense: stand for highs and mids, crouch for lows.

nodes.title: Frame advantage
nodes.why: On-block values say whose turn it is. Reading them is what turns a blocked move into a punish.

nodes.title: Standing punish ladder
nodes.why: Every blocked punishable move is free damage, but only if the right punisher comes out on reflex.

nodes.title: Crouching punishes
nodes.why: Blocking a low leaves Yoshimitsu crouching, and his while-standing punishers are a different ladder.

nodes.title: Throw breaks
nodes.why: Throws are unblockable guesses the opponent forces; breaking by the hands shown turns them into nothing.

nodes.title: Wake-up options
nodes.why: Getting up is a decision with its own risks: quickstand, rolls and tech rolls each lose to different answers.

nodes.title: Sidestep and sidewalk
nodes.why: Sidestepping makes linear moves whiff, which is the cheapest way to earn a punish against a predictable opponent.

nodes.title: Backdash and backdash cancel
nodes.why: The backdash cancel is Tekken movement in its purest form: space created on demand, without giving up the ability to act.

nodes.title: Whiff punishing
nodes.why: A whiffed move is a punish with no block required. Long tools like b+2,2, 3,1 and df+2 reach it.

nodes.title: Step block and dash block
nodes.why: Step block and dash block let Yoshimitsu advance and retreat while staying guarded, instead of walking into buttons.

nodes.title: Ten core moves
nodes.why: Ten moves carry almost every neutral situation Yoshimitsu will face; owning them on command is the core kit.

nodes.title: Standing punishers
nodes.why: Yoshimitsu's standing ladder runs from Flash at -6 to the Heat Smash at -18; each rung has exactly one best answer.

nodes.title: Crouching punishers
nodes.why: After blocking a low, ws4, ws1,2 and ws2,1 are the ladder: -11, -13 and -15, with ws2,1 launching.

nodes.title: Beginner combo to BnB
nodes.why: The bread-and-butter turns every launch into the same reliable damage, on both sides of the screen.

nodes.title: Wall and floor enders
nodes.why: Combos end at walls and floors, and the ender chosen there decides the next situation, not just the damage.

nodes.title: Verify core frame data
nodes.why: Seed data is unverified until it is checked in Practice. The conflict items from §10.14 are settled here, in the game.

nodes.title: Heat Burst or engage
nodes.why: Heat is a once-per-round resource. Entering it on purpose, by Burst or by Engager, is the whole skill.

nodes.title: His Heat Engagers
nodes.why: Five moves engage Heat: 3,1, f+1+2, b+2,2, KIN.f+2 and DGF.4. Hit-confirming them is what makes Heat reliable.

nodes.title: Heat Dash and Heat Smash
nodes.why: Heat Dash spends the gauge for +5g pressure and Heat Smash spends it all for damage and breaks; both are decisions, not habits.

nodes.title: Heat combos
nodes.why: Heat starters run one shared route. Learning it once covers H.f1+2f, H.b2,2f, H.DGF.4f and H.3,1f.

nodes.title: Heat powers (verify)
nodes.why: The claimed Heat powers, extra range, damage, chip and healing, predate the Season 2 nerf. They are verified in Practice, not believed.

nodes.title: Recoverable health and Rage
nodes.why: White health returns only by attacking, and Rage starts at 45 health since 3.02.01. Both change when to press and when to wait.

nodes.title: Flash punishes and interrupts
nodes.why: Flash at i6 is the fastest attack in the game. It punishes what everyone else must let go, and interrupts strings with gaps.

nodes.title: Flash frame traps
nodes.why: A counter-hit b+1 combos into Flash, and on block it is still a frame trap. The trap, not the Flash alone, is the skill.

nodes.title: Spin discipline
nodes.why: The Manji Spin evades almost everything and costs his own health. Used rarely, against linear strings, it is an escape; used often, it is a habit opponents punish.

nodes.title: Keepout spacing
nodes.why: Yoshimitsu wins by making opponents afraid to press. Max-range df+4, df+2, 3~4 and f+1+2 are the fence.

nodes.title: CD2 under highs
nodes.why: After df+1 (-4) or db+4 (-1), CD2 ducks under every high and launches on counter hit. It is the answer to opponents who press after minus frames.

nodes.title: Kincho parry
nodes.why: The Kincho parry (ps3-9) is a read on a high or mid. Throws, unblockables and charged moves beat it, so it is never a default.

nodes.title: DGF entries and plus routes
nodes.why: Dragonfly is entered with plus frames: holding up after 3,1, f,f,F+3 and 3~4. The entry, not the stance alone, creates the pressure.

nodes.title: DGF options
nodes.why: From Dragonfly, DGF.2, DGF.f+1+2, DGF.4 and DGF.3 are the mixup, and the random-guard dummy is the only honest judge of it.

nodes.title: Kincho pressure
nodes.why: Kincho pressure runs through 2,2 into KIN, then KIN.f+1+2, KIN.2 or KIN.d+1, with throws and the held version mixed in.

nodes.title: NSS routing and punishers
nodes.why: No Sword Stance changes the punishers: d+2,2,B routes into NSS, and 1,NSS.1 and 2,NSS.1 knock down or launch.

nodes.title: Frame traps
nodes.why: Frame traps turn plus frames into hits: f,f,F+3 and 3,1 into DGF.f+1+2, H.2+3 into DGF.4, Heat Dash into 1+2 or the 2+4 throw.

nodes.title: Wake-up reads and tech-roll punish
nodes.why: Tech rolls are punished by FC.DF+1, wake-up kicks are -9 on block, and side rolls are caught by homing moves. The read is the skill.

nodes.title: Unblockable setups and weak sides
nodes.why: Unblockables have weak sides: sword right, spit left. They are reads, not habits, and the weak side is what makes them land.

nodes.title: Guard-break setup
nodes.why: Ending with KIN.(2),1+2* guard-breaks for a free b+2,2 on stand-up, or counter-hits wake-up kicks.

nodes.title: Stances II tour
nodes.why: FLE, IND, MED, BT and BDS complete the stance map. Each has one fastest option and one honest counter.

nodes.title: MED cancel (needs a source)
nodes.why: The MED cancel is listed as a key technique, but the Wavu tech page is empty. It stays marked needs a source until a reliable description is found.

nodes.title: Staple and wall combos
nodes.why: The staple route and the wall enders are the combos that win rounds in real matches, drilled until they survive pressure.

nodes.title: Replay review habit
nodes.why: Three reviewed replays per ten games is the habit that turns losses into matchup sheets instead of frustration.

nodes.title: Sheets for the 10 most-faced characters
nodes.why: A matchup sheet is three problem moves with answers, a plan against turtling and a plan against aggression, for each character actually faced.

nodes.title: Problem-move lab
nodes.why: Each problem move becomes a lab drill: record it, then apply the answer until the answer is the reflex.

nodes.title: Anti-turtle and anti-aggression plans
nodes.why: Turtles are opened with plus-frame routes, throws, Kincho mixups and oki unblockables; aggression is answered with keepout, Flash and the spin, used sparingly.

nodes.title: Advanced tech from sourced guides
nodes.why: Advanced technique enters the library only from sourced guides, with provenance attached, never from rumor.

nodes.title: Patch adaptation
nodes.why: Every patch re-verifies the moves it changed. Changed moves become sourced again, their cards come due, and one verify task is queued.

nodes.title: Tournament preparation
nodes.why: Tournament preparation is the same loop under pressure: a plan, a warm-up, and a review after every set.

nodes.title: Personal style library
nodes.why: The personal style library is the record of what actually works for Sagar: the routes, traps and oki setups his own data supports.

drills.title: Decode 10 inputs

Name the directions, buttons and connectors.
Score 8 of 10 to pass.
progressions: Add the P2 side, then randomize the dummy order.
regressions: Reduce to one side and a fixed dummy until the target is met.

recipe: Record the dummy doing a low and a mid.

steps: Block standing until you see the low, then crouch.
Do not guess: react to the move.
Log each rep as blocked or hit.
progressions: Add the P2 side, then randomize the dummy order.
